title: The Road Home - Werner Forssmann, 1929
look: premium historical science documentary: art-directed 3D, low-key motivated lighting, period-accurate 1929 Germany, tasteful anatomical cutaways

palette.1929: warm tungsten amber + cool window daylight, desaturated greens and creams of hospital paint, deep brown wood
palette.anatomy: near-black void, blue-violet veins, deep red heart, warm amber catheter, cool rim
palette.xray: blue-grey radiographic film, cold light-box white, grain
palette.1956: gold and burgundy, elegant soft key

continuity.forssmann_young: 25, slim, dark hair slicked back with a side part, clean-shaven, white surgical coat over waistcoat and tie, dark trousers; the catheter always enters his LEFT inner elbow
continuity.forssmann_old: 52, same face, grey hair, round glasses, dark suit; tailcoat on the Nobel stage
continuity.chief: 60s, grey hair, grey moustache, round glasses, dark suit under an open white coat
continuity.nurse: 30s, white 1920s uniform dress, white cap, keys on a ring at her belt
continuity.surgeon_berlin: famous surgeon (unnamed in VO), 50s, bald crown, moustache, dark three-piece suit
continuity.catheter: thin amber-brown varnished rubber ureteral catheter, about 65 cm, coiled on an enamel tray before use
continuity.screen_direction: Forssmann's journey moves screen-left to screen-right (arm -> heart, office -> OR -> X-ray room)

sequences.name: Hook - the impossible question
sequences.takeaway: A doctor pushed a tube into his own heart - and the question is how he lived

sequences.name: 1929 - the belief
sequences.takeaway: In 1929, medicine treated the inside of a living heart as untouchable

sequences.name: The refusal
sequences.takeaway: A young junior doctor asks; his powerful boss refuses

sequences.name: The nurse's rule
sequences.takeaway: He goes anyway; the nurse with the keys agrees only if he tries it on her

sequences.name: The trick
sequences.takeaway: He straps her down and numbs her arm, then secretly cuts his own

sequences.name: The tube goes in
sequences.takeaway: The tube enters a vein at the elbow and is pushed more than half a metre toward the chest

sequences.name: The blind spot
sequences.takeaway: He can't see where it went, so he walks, tube inside him, to the X-ray room

sequences.name: The reveal
sequences.takeaway: The X-ray shows the tip inside his heart - and he is alive

sequences.name: The ridicule
sequences.takeaway: He expected praise; a famous surgeon dismissed it as a circus stunt

sequences.name: The quiet years
sequences.takeaway: Years later he was a small-town bladder doctor, not a heart doctor

sequences.name: The payoff
sequences.takeaway: 27 years after that walk, the Nobel Prize

sequences.name: Today
sequences.takeaway: Heart catheters are now routine, every day

sequences.name: The road home
sequences.takeaway: Veins are roads to the heart - he didn't break in, he followed the road

shots.vo: How did a doctor push a tube
shots.purpose: Introduce THE object of the story: the thin tube, in a 1929 operating room, being pushed forward
shots.visible: Macro: coiled amber rubber catheter on a white enamel instrument tray beside a scalpel and syringe; the tube slides forward off the coil as if fed by an unseen hand
shots.action: Catheter end slides ~6 cm toward camera
shots.environment: OR side table, steel and enamel, defocused tiled wall and the big surgical lamp disc as bokeh

camera.move: low macro slide along the tube toward its tip, rack focus coil -> tip

lighting.notes: one hard top-down surgical spot, deep falloff, cool tile bounce, specular streak along the varnished tube

shots.transition_out: match: the tube's line continues into the glowing vein of the next shot (same screen direction left->right)

shots.purpose: Show the absurd destination: the tube runs from the arm to the heart inside a living man
shots.visible: Translucent upper body (ghost skin) with blue veins, faint ribcage, red heart; the amber catheter traced from the left elbow up the arm into the chest
shots.action: Heart beats (lub-dub) as the camera arrives at it
shots.environment: Black studio void with gentle haze

camera.move: crane down and in from the shoulder along the catheter to the heart

lighting.notes: cool blue rim on the ghost skin, warm key on the heart, haze

shots.purpose: Stakes: a living, beating heart with a foreign tube touching it
shots.visible: Extreme close-up of the heart's right atrium, catheter tip resting in it, heart beating once with a light pulse

camera.move: slow push into the heart, focus on the catheter tip

lighting.notes: warm key from above-left, red SSS glow, deep shadow side

shots.connects: The rule -> the young man who will break it

shots.title: Werner Forssmann · 25

shots.title: according to his memoir

shots.title: 60 cm

shots.vo: There was one problem. He couldn't see where the tube had gone.
shots.purpose: The human beat: he looks at the tube vanishing into his arm and has no idea where its tip is
shots.visible: Medium to close: Forssmann at the trolley looking down at the tube vanishing into his elbow, then toward his chest
shots.action: Glances from the arm toward his chest on 'where' (42.29)

camera.move: slow push from arm up to his eyes

lighting.notes: single warm key from the lamp, cool rim, half his face in shadow

shots.connects: Problem -> solution: walk to the X-ray

shots.vo: So, with it still inside him, he walked to the X-ray room.
shots.purpose: The walk: tube inside him, he walks to the room marked RÖNTGEN
shots.visible: Leading dolly in front of him: Forssmann walks toward camera holding his left arm, the tube taped along it; camera turns as he passes to reveal the door sign 'RÖNTGEN' at the corridor's end
shots.action: Walk; door sign revealed on 'X-ray room' (46.66)

camera.move: dolly back ahead of him, then pan 120 degrees as he passes to reveal the door

shots.transition_out: light-based: the door's glow fills frame -> X-ray room

shots.purpose: The film comes out; the moment of truth

shots.vo: The tip of the tube was sitting inside his heart.

shots.environment: Film on the light box (emulsion texture, clip, edge)

camera.move: slow push from the whole film to the heart and tip

lighting.notes: backlit film, cool

shots.purpose: Emotional beat: he is alive; quiet awe

shots.vo: Years later, he wasn't even a heart doctor.

shots.title: Nobel Prize · 1956

shots.vo: Today, doctors slide tubes into hearts every single day.

shots.vo: Every vein in your arm is a road that leads back to your heart.
